standard_prerequisites.name: The flattening map theorem, representing the locus where a map of modules becomes an isomorphism
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, label theorem-flattening-map (invoked at proof line 6777)
standard_prerequisites.use: Applied to the surjection $u : \mathcal{O}_X \to \mathcal{O}_X/\mathcal{I}$, it represents by a closed immersion $Z \to S$ the $T$ for which $u_T$ is an isomorphism, which is exactly the Weil restriction functor $F$.

standard_prerequisites.name: The ideal sheaf of a closed subscheme and the associated surjection
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, the ideal sheaf $\mathcal{I}$ of $Y$ in $X$ (used at proof lines 6772-6773)
standard_prerequisites.use: It converts the condition that $Y_T \to X_T$ be an isomorphism into the condition that the pullback $u_T$ of the surjection be an isomorphism.

core_obligations: Introduce the ideal sheaf $\mathcal{I}$ defining $Y$ in $X$ and the surjection $u : \mathcal{O}_X \to \mathcal{O}_X/\mathcal{I}$ (proof lines 6772-6773).

Observe that for an $S$-scheme $T$ the closed immersion $Y_T \to X_T$ is an isomorphism if and only if $u_T$ is an isomorphism, so the functor $F$ is the locus where $u_T$ is an isomorphism (proof lines 6774-6775).

Apply the flattening map theorem to represent $F$ by a closed immersion $Z \to S$, and read off that $Z \to S$ is of finite presentation when $Y \to S$ is (proof lines 6776-6777 and statement lines 6767-6768).
proof_roadmap: The ideal sheaf and its surjection (proof lines 6772-6773).
Translation of the isomorphism condition (proof lines 6774-6775).
Representation by the theorem and the finite presentation clause (proof lines 6776-6777).
difficulty_reason: The lemma represents the Weil restriction of a closed subscheme along a flat pure morphism of finite presentation by a closed immersion, with the finite presentation clause inherited from the subscheme (statement lines 6752-6769). The proof encodes the subscheme through the ideal sheaf and its surjection, observes that being an isomorphism for $Y_T \to X_T$ is the same as for the pulled back surjection, and invokes the flattening map theorem. The translation of the condition is the substance, so the claim is H2.
